messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert - high error rate and crashloops detected in serving-runtime autoscale group 'gpu-pool-a'. Pager routed to @maya (oncall). Root metric: token-generation 5xx spike from 00:23 UTC.

maya (oncall): Acknowledged. Investigating. Any recent deploys?

sam (runtime): No deploys in last 30m. I'm seeing lots of OOMKilled and repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in the runtime logs for model-worker pods. Pasting tail:
```
I0325 00:22:38 model-worker[pid=2142]: RuntimeError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
I0325 00:22:39 kubelet: Pod model-worker-7fb9 OOMKilled
I0325 00:22:40 kubelet: BackOff restarting failed container
```

jared (infra): Noted node flaps too - nodes in that pool temporarily go NotReady then back, autoscaler then scales up more pods, which causes GPU memory contention -> more OOMs. Looks like rapid scale-up/scale-down (thrash).

lina (sre): Can someone dump the HPA/autoscaler events? 

sam (runtime): `kubectl get hpa -n serving gpu-runtime-hpa -o yaml` shows scaleDown stabilization window low and minReplicas=1, maxReplicas=12. Events:
```
Events:
  ScalingReplicaSet ... scaled up from 2 to 8 (reason: CPUUtilization)
  ScalingReplicaSet ... scaled down from 8 to 2 (reason: CPUUtilization)
```

maya (oncall): So autoscaler is oscillating between <3 and >8 rapidly. That explains thrash. Proposal: temporarily pause autoscaler and set replicas to a safe fixed value to stabilize. Suggest `kubectl scale deploy gpu-runtime --replicas=6 -n serving` and annotate HPA to pause.

rob (eng-runtime): +1. Also we should disable experimental continuous-batching for these pods until memory profiling is done. That feature increases per-process KV cache which might push memory beyond GPU capacity during scale spikes.

jared (infra): I'll cordon two flaky nodes and drain pods off them to stop node flaps: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-8-12` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets ip-10-0-8-12`.

emma (support): Customer impact check - I'm seeing tickets for slow/failed completions for chat-gen and embeddings endpoints. ETA on mitigation? Customers affected: internal account metrics (team-saas-prod), and a handful of high-traffic API keys. We should update status page.

maya (oncall): Action list: 1) Pause autoscaler / fix replica count to 6 (jared) 2) Cordon/fluid draining of flaky nodes (jared) 3) Disable continuous-batching on gpu-runtime config (rob) 4) Restart runtime pods gracefully (sam) 5) Post status update (emma).

jared (infra): Scaling to 6 now: `kubectl scale deploy gpu-runtime --replicas=6 -n serving` -> scaled. Annotating HPA: `kubectl annotate hpa gpu-runtime autoscaler.kubernetes.io/paused=true -n serving`.

ops-bot: Action recorded: autoscaler paused (annotation added) by jared at 00:28 UTC. Replica set targeted to 6.

lina (sre): After scaling, we need to monitor OOMs and GPU memory usage. Sam, can you tail `nvidia-smi` logs and pod memory?

sam (runtime): Tailing memory: GPUs are at 98% on some nodes right after scale, but with fixed replicas the pressure is steady and OOMKill rate drops. I'm seeing fewer `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` now.

rob (eng-runtime): I pushed a hotfix to disable continuous-batching via configmap toggle: `kubectl patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"continuous_batching":"false"}}' -n serving`. New pods should pick it up on restart.

maya (oncall): Sam, please restart pods gradually to pick up config: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/gpu-runtime -n serving --timeout=5m` — do rolling restart to avoid mass churn.

sam (runtime): Rolling restart in progress. Watching logs for errors.

emma (support): Posting status: "Degraded - Serving runtime experiencing elevated errors and latency. Mitigation underway. Some API requests may receive 5xx. Engineers actively investigating." Will include estimated ETA 30-45m.

jared (infra): After drain and cordon, two nodes had kernel Oops on GPU driver leading to flaps. I've tainted them `NoSchedule` until we confirm driver stability.

lina (sre): Good call. We'll open a ticket with cloud infra to replace or repro the driver Oops. For now keep autoscaler paused. We'll also increase stabilization window to avoid immediate resuming.

maya (oncall): Quick customer-impact summary for on-call report: - Affected services: chat-gen, embeddings (multi-tenant). - Symptom: 5xx/timeout and increased latency. - Root cause (initial): GPU driver/node instability causing node flaps -> autoscaler thrash -> memory pressure and OOM/CUDA errors -> crashloops. - Mitigation: paused autoscaler, fixed replica count to 6, cordoned flaky nodes, disabled continuous-batching, rolling restart. - Severity: SEV2.

rob (eng-runtime): We should also ensure fallback to smaller model variant for affected tenants temporarily to reduce per-request memory. Can we flip routing policy?

sam (runtime): We can set runtime-routing feature flag `model_variant_fallback=true` for high-traffic keys. Doing that for `team-saas-prod` now.

ops-bot: Feature flag `model_variant_fallback` toggled for 3 API keys by sam at 00:42 UTC.

emma (support): Updating customers that we've mitigated immediate instability and are monitoring. Will follow up with RCA timeline.

maya (oncall): Monitoring for 15 minutes. If OOMs stay low and latency improves, we'll consider unpausing autoscaler with higher minReplicas and larger stabilization window. Lina, can you own the postmortem?

lina (sre): I'll own the postmortem and schedule a follow-up retro. Items to include: autoscaler tuning (stabilization windows, min/max), continuous-batching memory accounting, node driver health checks, and improved canarying for kernel/driver updates.

jared (infra): After 10m, node flaps stopped, new pods stable. No further `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`.

maya (oncall): All right - status update: incident mitigation successful for now. Keeping autoscaler paused for next 2 hours while we monitor. Transfer to post-incident: @lina leading RCA. Handing off primary to @lina for 02:00 UTC shift. I'll do the ops notes and close the pager.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: 'autoscale-thrash-gpu' severity SEV2. Primary oncall: maya. Owner for RCA: lina.

emma (support): Final note — I've escalated affected customer tickets to priority and offered temporary rate-limits/fallbacks where appropriate. I'll coordinate postmortem customer comms with Lina.

maya (oncall): Thanks team. I'll stand down but remain reachable.

lina (sre): A quick follow-up action item list I'll add to the postmortem: 1) Increase HPA stabilization windows and minReplicas to avoid thrash. 2) Add GPU driver health probe and auto-replace node when kernel Oops detected. 3) Add memory-usage-based autoscaling metric (not just CPU). 4) Add canary gating for continuous-batching and driver updates. 5) Create runbook for autoscale-thrash incidents.

jared (infra): I'll own node replacement and driver repro. Provide a link to the node crash dump when ready.

sam (runtime): I'll run memory-profiling on continuous-batching and produce a patch to limit KV cache per-process.

incident-bot: Thread closed by maya (oncall) at 00:58 UTC.
